profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 93 (NTT Dallas cluster, further attempt): operators own overview page confirms Dallas TX1 and TX4 buildings and a 124 MW planned campus but no addresses, dedicated pages 404. Two of four rows geocoded to Lookout Dr, Garland, TX, assessed as likely residential rather than the actual campus and not applied, alongside an unconfirmed Telecom Parkway alternate. research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete for all four rows, no address applied to any.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to NTT, part of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, one of the largest telecommunications and IT services groups in the world, headquartered in Tokyo, Japan. NTT operates a global data center business, NTT Global Data Centers, under NTT DATA, Inc. The operators own about us page, fetched this session, states NTT DATA is a top 10 global IT services provider with about 30 billion dollars in annual revenue, operations across 33 countries, and about 3 billion dollars in annual research and development investment, headquartered at the Toyosu Center Building, 3-3-3 Toyosu, Koto-ku, Tokyo 135-6033, Japan, though these figures describe the wider NTT DATA organization rather than the data center division specifically, and no data center division formation or acquisition date was found on the pages fetched this session. A previously confirmed, specific data center acquisition remains NTT Communications purchase of an 86.7 percent stake in e-shelter, described as Germany top data center operator, completed around June 23, 2015, though that acquisition is not directly connected to this United States facility. This session reached the operators own services.global.ntt data center locations pages directly and successfully. An earlier sessions attempts to reach the ragingwire.com domain had failed and found no corresponding Wikipedia article, a negative finding this session did not need to repeat. The operators own current Dallas area locations overview page, fetched this session, names two buildings, Dallas TX1 Data Center and Dallas TX4 Data Center, and states a planned 124 MW IT load once the campus is fully built out, but gives no street address for either. Dedicated TX1 and TX4 facility pages, guessed from the naming pattern used successfully elsewhere for this operator, both returned 404. Reverse geocoding two of this four row clusters own coordinates through a third party service returned addresses on Lookout Dr in Garland, TX, at 0.9 confidence each, though at wider distances than typical for a confident match, and the tightly spaced, small increment numbering seen among the candidate and nearby alternate addresses on that street, for example 1788, 1792, 1796, 1800, and 1908, reads as consistent with an ordinary residential subdivision rather than a data center campus. One geocode response also surfaced an unconfirmed alternate candidate, 7200 Telecom Parkway in nearby Richardson, TX, a street name more thematically consistent with a telecom or data facility, but this was not independently confirmed by a second geocode point or any other source. Given the residential character of the primary candidate street and the lack of a confirming second source for either candidate, this session does not apply an address to any row in this four row cluster.

reading.body:
NTT operates a planned 124 MW data center campus in the Dallas area with two buildings, Dallas TX1 and Dallas TX4, but publishes no street address and the operator's dedicated pages for each building return 404 errors. The campus specifications are stated only on an overview page that names the buildings and total planned IT load. The exact physical location in Garland or nearby Richardson cannot be confirmed from available published sources.

At 40 kW per rack, a common density for AI training, 124 MW of planned IT load translates to roughly 3,100 racks, assuming the figure denotes IT load rather than total facility power draw. This would place the campus among the larger published facilities in Texas if fully built, but no incremental capacity milestones or occupancy timeline are published. No certifications for the campus are published.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities of which only 18 publish capacity figures totaling 468 MW. This campus would rank 19th by published MW in the state if built as planned, sitting just outside the published-capacity tier. The campus does not appear on this site's mapped facilities list because its address remains unconfirmed despite research effort, limiting its use in assessing the current grid constraint on AI scaling in Texas.
